newsitem.title: EGYPT: Exiled Egyptian militant denies recruiting Algerian.
newsitem.headline: Exiled Egyptian militant denies recruiting Algerian.

text.p: An exiled Egyptian Moslem militant on Friday denied charges by Egypt's Interior Ministry that he had sent an Algerian woman to Cairo with money and orders to his comrades to stage violent attacks.
Yasser Tawfiq Ali el-Serri said in a statement faxed to an international news agency from London that he challenged Egyptian authorities to prove their allegations.
The Interior Ministry on Thursday said police had arrested Djamila al-Falaki on Wednesday with money, a firearm and literature of the violent Jihad (Holy War) group in her possession.
It said she had tried to contact three lawyers who were members of the group, which assassinated president Anwar Sadat in 1981.
"I deny the charges of Egyptian authorities that I recruited this woman or that I sent her from London to Egypt," Serri said.
"I defy the authorities to prove these allegations and to say when she left Britain and entered Egypt," he added.
The Interior Ministry did not say that Falaki had come to Egypt from Britain.
The ministry said Serri was a leading member of Jihad. He is on the run from several jail terms in Egypt and a death sentence for trying to kill former prime minister Atef Sedki in 1993.
He is the director of the International Islamic Observatory which projects the Islamic point of view on Middle Eastern affairs.

Jihad is one of several militant groups fighting to topple the Egyptian government and set up a strict Islamic state. More than 1,000 people have been killed in political violence since militants began their anti-government campaign in 1992.
